# notecase

LNURLcash (LUD-25) wallet for Node 22+: receive, hold, split, merge, send
and melt Lightning bearer notes. CLI plus a reusable engine. ESM-only. MIT.

Install: not yet on npm - build from source (see README)
Companion mint: @forgesworn/moneyer
Protocol client it builds on: lnurlcash-kit
Draft spec: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/pull/301

## The rules the engine enforces (and any wallet MUST)

1. Persist before disclose: a replacement secret reaches disk BEFORE its
   hash goes on the wire. Use the kit's *WithHash variants, never the
   generating ones, if you care about crashes.
2. Only a DEFINITIVE rejection discards a staged secret. Timeouts, broken
   JSON, dropped connections and unconfirmed 200s all keep it, parked as
   ambiguous, until a probe of the mint proves what happened.
3. Melt OK means in flight. The note locks; settlement is confirmed via
   LUD-21 verify, and a failed melt is recovered by a rotate probe - safe
   in every outcome by construction.
4. Rotate immediately on receive and on mint claim: the previous holder
   (or anyone who saw the invoice) still knows the old secret.
5. maxWithdrawable from the informational GET is the note's value; the
   URL's amount parameter is an unverified claim.
6. Pin mint pubkeys on first use; refuse hard on a change. A `sig` that
   does not verify against the pin is a REFUSAL (BadSignatureError), not a
   warning - overridable only per receive. No `sig` at all is a warning.
7. Verify NWC payments by preimage against the invoice's payment hash -
   a successful-looking response is not evidence money moved.
8. Never print, log or echo a k1 except on explicit send/export.
9. Offline is a promise, not a guess. Never infer it from connectivity:
   an offline send makes no wire call at all, and an offline receive
   verifies the mint's signature against a pinned key or refuses. A note
   taken that way is stored unrotated and rotated by the next reconcile.
10. Sweep every note against its mint from time to time: a bearer note has
   copies, and one burned out of band stays listed as money until asked
   about. A mint that does not answer is never marked on.

## CLI

notecase init [--insecure-plaintext]
notecase mints add <address|lnurl> / list / use <host>
notecase mint <sats> [--manual] [--mint <host>]
notecase receive <note> [--force] | send <sats> | melt <bolt11 | sats --to <addr> | sats --to-nwc>
notecase check [--apply] [--mint <host>]
notecase ladder [set <sats,...>] [--copies n] | prepare [--apply]
notecase send <sats> --offline [--overpay] | receive --offline
notecase balance | list [--all] | reconcile | verify <note>
notecase nwc set <uri> / status / clear
notecase backup export | shares [--threshold N --count M] | recover-key

Amounts are sats (--msat for msat). PIN via prompt or $NOTECASE_PIN.
NOTECASE_HOME relocates the store; NOTECASE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1 admits LAN mints.

## Library API

openWallet({pin?, home?}) / initWallet(...) -> {data, save, encrypted, storeKey}
new Wallet(data, save, {fetch?, timeoutMs?}) ->
  receive(input, {acceptBadSignature?}), send(amountMsat), prepareExact(amountMsat),
  melt(pr, target), startMint(grossMsat), claimMint(pending, preimage),
  awaitMint(pending), reconcile(), checkNotes({apply?, mintHost?}) -> CheckReport,
  balanceMsat(), unrotatedMsat(), verifyNoteOffline(input), addMint(input),
  ladderFor(host), setLadder(host, sats[], copies), ladderPlan(host) -> LadderPlan,
  prepareOffline(host), planOfflineSend(msat, host?) -> OfflineSelection,
  sendOffline(msat, host?, {acceptOverpay?}), receiveOffline(input)
createWalletFetch({allowPrivate?}) - DNS-pinned fetch, loopback passthrough
payWithNwc(uri, pr) / invoiceFromNwc(uri, amountMsat, desc) / nwcStatus(uri)

All amounts are integer milli-satoshis in the engine; the CLI speaks sats.
